The Brown kestrel (Falco berigora) is a medium-sized raptor widely distributed across Australia and New Guinea, occupying a range of open and semi-arid habitats. Field measurements of newly hatched chicks indicate a wet weight at birth of approximately 31 grams [Wwb = approximately 31 grams], a value that reflects the considerable yolk investment characteristic of falconids. Comparative data from Broome and the Kimberley region suggest that the initial wet weight of the egg, measured immediately after laying, is around 45 grams [Ww0 = around 45 grams], representing a substantial proportional investment relative to the adult female's body mass.
